sentences.text:
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Suman R.,
in the road traffic accident that took place on 30.01.2021.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 30.01.2021 at about 2.00 p.m. when the deceased was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HL-3940, Bommasandra Dmart, Hebbagodi P.S., at that time the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-D-3115 by driving the same Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
2 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle from behind,
caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

Immediately after the accident, deceased was shifted to Sparsh hospital, wherein post-mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards hospital and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was working in a private company and earning Rs.20,416/- per month.

The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony, lost love and affection of their son and brother and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-D-3115.
Hence, the 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed written statements.

5. The respondent No.1, in his objection statement contended that he insured his vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-D- 3115 with second respondent vide policy No.0704433118P1172 valid from 31.03.2020 to 30.03.2021.
If the tribunal comes to the conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for the compensation, same may be saddled on the 2nd respondent.
It is further contended that there was no negligence of drive of the Tipper Lorry.
Hence on all these grounds, he has sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. The 2nd respondent in its objection statement has denied all the petition averments and contended that the petition itself is not maintainable either on facts or law.

It has denied the age,
income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-D-3115 and liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Suman R. has died in the road traffic accident occurred on 30.01.2021 at about 2.00 p.m. near Bommasandra D Mart, Hebbagodi P.S. due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/

3 Tipper lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-D-3115?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
3
. What order or Award?
8. In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P1 to 14.
Also examined one witness as PW.2 and he got marked documents as per Ex.P15 to P.17.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any defence evidence.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 30.01.2021 at about 2.00 p.m. when the deceased was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HL-3940, Bommasandra Dmart,
Hebbagodi P.S., at that time the driver of the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-D-3115 by driving the same came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle from behind, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

12. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, sketch, Inquest Report, P.M. Report, IMV Report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
13.
On the other hand, the version of the petitioners remains unchallenged and undisputed.
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
14. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.

There are four basic elements that a person Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
4 has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

15. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Bommasandra D-Mart,
Bangalore-Hosur road, NH-7 Service Road. when the driver of Tipper lorry came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex . P.1
FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar and Ex.P4 Sketch prepared at the time of mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding in his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the Tipper lorry came in a negligent manner from back side and hit the motor cyclist.
The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of Tipper lorry had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.7 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 4, 7 coupled with Ex.P.8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Tipper lorry driver.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/

5 preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the bus is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.

17. Further though PW.1 was cross examined by respondent counsel at length, nothing is elicited from her mouth with regard to the negligence on the part of deceased and on the other hand the petitioners with the help of Ex.P3, P4, P5 coupled with Ex.P8 clearly demonstrated that there is a negligence on the part of offending vehicle driver.
Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-D-3115 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of Suman R., was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
KA-51-D-3115.
The petitioner No.1 is stated to be the father and petitioner No.2 stated to be mother, and petitioner No.3 stated to be sister of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of the petitioners at Ex's.P.11 to 13 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.

Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was aged 24 years at the time of accident.

The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the age of the deceased, hence this court has Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
6 relied on the PM report marked at Ex.P6 which reflects the age of the deceased as 24 years.
The accident was occurred in the year 2021.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 24 years.

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, considering the age of the deceased, the multiplier applicable to the age of 24 years is 18.
20.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as GDA at Terrier security Services (I) Pvt. Ltd., as security guard and earning Rs.23,000/- per month.
On order to prove the same, petitioners have produced ID card issued by the said company at Ex.P14.
Also examined the Manager of the Terrier security Services (I) Pvt. Ltd.,. as PW.2 and he got marked Employment ID, Adhaar card of PW.2 and Salary receipt at at Ex.P15 to 17.

entities.text: Manager of the Terrier security Services (I) Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: The documents produced by the petitioners, as well as PW.2 depicts that deceased was the employee of the company.

On perusal of the Ex.P17 Salary slips, petitioner has earned net salary of Rs.21,868/- in the month of October 2020, Rs.22,466/- in the month of November 2020 and in the month of December 2020 Rs.21,311/-.
There is variation in salary of the deceased.
Hence, average income of Rs.22,065/- is taken into consideration for calculation of loss of dependency.
Income of the deceased does not come under the income tax slab for deducting of income tax.
Hence, the annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.2,64,780/- p.a.

In view of principles laid down in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680), as deceased was below the age of 40 years and was on fixed salary,
an addition of 40% of the actual salary towards future prospectus is to be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 40% on the annual income of Rs.2,64,780/- comes to Rs.1,05,912/-.
21. In the case on hand, the deceased died leaving behind 3 dependents and he was a bachelor.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009 ACJ 1298)., 50%(1/2) of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.1,85,346/- per annum (Rs.3,70,692 - Rs.1,85,346/-)
22.

entities.text: Sarla Varma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009 ACJ 1298)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,85,346/- p.a. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.33,36,228/- (Rs.1,85,346 X 18).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.33,36,228/- under the head of Loss of dependency.
23. In this case, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and petitioner No.3 is the unmarried sister of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.

Therefore, petitioner No.1 to 3 are Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
7 entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

24. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners have produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.2,24,664/- at Ex.P10.

On perusal of said bills, it does not reflect the seal and signature of the Sparsh hospital,
nor it is taken in the letter head of the said hospital.
Hence the said bills are not considered for paying compensation under this head.

26. The calculation table stands as follows :
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.33,36,228/-
 2. Towards loss of Filial Consortium Rs.1,32,000/-
 (44,000x3)
 3. Towards loss to Estate Rs.16,500/-
 4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.16,500/-
 body funeral and obsequies  ceremony expenses  5.

Medical Expenses Nil.
 Total Rs.35,01,228/-
In all the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,01,228/-.

26. As regard the apportionment of the compensation, petitioners No.1 to 3 father, mother and sister of the deceased. Therefore out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 30:50:20.
27.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.2 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.

Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
8 28.
Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-D-3115.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,01,228/- (Rupees Thirty five lakhs one thousand two hundred and twenty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 30% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Petitioner No.3 - 20% Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 it reflects that deceased was proceeding in his lane on the left side of the road and suddenly the Tipper lorry came in a negligent manner from back side and hit the motor cyclist.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P.3, 4, 7 coupled with Ex.P.8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Tipper lorry driver.
5 preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
19.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the age of the deceased, hence this court has Rangaswamy B.R vs Venkatesh Murthy on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15639593/
6 relied on the PM report marked at Ex.P6 which reflects the age of the deceased as 24 years.
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case rendered in National Insurance Co., Ltd.,
vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680) has held that, age of the deceased is basis for applying the multiplier.
Hence, average income of Rs.22,065/- is taken into consideration for calculation of loss of dependency.
Income of the deceased does not come under the income tax slab for deducting of income tax.
In view of principles laid down in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and others ((2017) 16 SCC 680), as deceased was below the age of 40 years and was on fixed salary,
an addition of 40% of the actual salary towards future prospectus is to be considered.
As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009 ACJ 1298)., 50%(1/2) of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.1,85,346/- per annum (Rs.3,70,692 - Rs.1,85,346/-)
22.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and family members to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
24. Further, as law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to the estate, funeral expenses and consortium to be awarded.

29. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,01,228/- (Rupees Thirty five lakhs one thousand two hundred and twenty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 30% Petitioner No.2 - 50% Petitioner No.3 - 20% Out of the share amount of Petitioners No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
